title: Robust Multi-Objective Controlled Decoding of Large Language Models
claim: Prior multi-objective decoding needs user-given weights and can leave one objective poor; ours computes worst-case weights to give balanced, robust outputs.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right flow, paired reward bar charts at right ends
description: Two side-by-side panels with matching diagrams. The left panel, titled 'Conventional Multi-Objective Decoding (MOD)', shows given weights (w1,w2,w3) and a prompt x feeding a rounded box that holds value-function chips V1-V3 above an LLM block. An arrow leads to a 'Non-robust' output y. Next to it is a bar chart of rewards r1, r2, r3 (magenta, red, green), where the red bar is very short and a yellow arrow marks it as the worst case. The right panel, titled 'Robust Multi-Objective Decoding (RMOD)' with 'Robust' highlighted in a blue box, has the same box with an empty-set symbol and x as inputs. It outputs robust weights w* ('Compute robust'), then a 'Robust' y. Its bar chart has balanced bars lifted above a dashed line. The eye goes first to the colored bars, then to the contrast between the two bar charts.
caption: (Left) Existing multi-objective alignment methods require the weights for each reward. (Right) RMOD produces a robust response $y$ when a prompt $x$ is given, using the value functions for each objective $V_i$ and the worst-case weights $w^*$ computed by solving a min-max problem.
abstract: We introduce Robust Multi-Objective Decoding (RMOD), a novel inference-time algorithm that robustly aligns Large Language Models (LLMs) to multiple human objectives (e.g., instruction-following, helpfulness, safety) by maximizing the worst-case rewards. RMOD formulates the robust decoding problem as a maximin two-player game between adversarially computed reward weights and the sampling policy, solvable through a Nash equilibrium. We demonstrate that this game reduces to a convex optimization problem to identify the worst-case reward weights, with the optimal sampling policy analytically derived. For practical applications, we propose an efficient algorithm of RMOD tailored for contemporary LLMs, introducing minimal computational overhead compared to standard non-robust Controlled Decoding methods. Experimental results across a range of popular alignment datasets with up to 10 objectives show the effectiveness of RMOD and its distilled version, consistently outperforming baselines in worst-case rewards and win rates.
